title: Investigating the efficacy of a short-intervention implementing chairwork in students with test anxiety - A randomised controlled study.
summary:
The aim of this study is to examine the extent to which the experience-oriented, emotion-focused technique called chair work alters symptoms associated with test anxiety in pupils/students, by implementing a short stand-alone treatment. On one hand, it will be examined to what extent the handling of inner critical voices (self-criticism) and self-compassion changes. On the other hand, it will be investigated to what extent chair work improves the ability to regulate emotions, and enhances self-esteem, and to what extent subjective and objectively measurable test anxiety can be reduced.  

Within chairwork, patients become increasingly aware of inner parts of the self, which are placed on different chairs to become emotionally palpable for the patient. On the one hand, chairwork aims to reduce the avoidance of unpleasant feelings and to promote healthy emotion regulation. For another, to bring out dysfunctional cognitions in a centralized way and replace them with more appropriate thoughts through questioning. For example, a situation of a student with test anxiety who does not show up for an exam could be used. One of the chairs could symbolize the patient's thoughts or self-critical voices (e.g. "I won't make it anyway", " I will fail"), while another chair captures the patient's emotions (fear, despair). In a further step, these inner parts interact dialogically with the help of the therapist in such a way that a more functional solution for the behavior in the situation can be found.
conditions: PAF (Test Anxiety Questionnaire) sum score above the cut-off: values of T > 60

interventions.name: Intervention group "chairwork": Participants receive a total of three therapy sessions using chairwork over the course of three weeks (one session per week, approx. 90 minutes each).
